A.title: Why does Qwen3-8B Q6_K_L run slowly on a TitanXP with 32GB RAM in LM Studio?
A.body:
I've come across a report from May 2025 where a user ran Qwen3-8B Q6_K_L in LM Studio on a system with a TitanXP GPU (12GB VRAM) and 32GB of RAM, but experienced very slow and odd behavior. Given that 12GB VRAM is somewhat limited for larger quantized models, I wonder if the bottleneck might be related to VRAM constraints or how LM Studio handles this quantization type.

Has anyone else tried running Qwen3-8B Q6_K_L on similar hardware and noticed performance issues? Are there known quirks with LM Studio's support for Q6_K_L quantization that could cause slowdowns or instability on GPUs like the TitanXP? Any practical advice on settings or workarounds would be appreciated.

B.title: Why is Qwen3-8B Q6_K_L so slow and odd in LM Studio on a TitanXP setup?
B.body: I came across a detailed user report from May 2025 about running Qwen3-8B with Q6_K_L quantization in LM Studio on a system with a TitanXP GPU (12GB VRAM) and 32GB RAM. The user describes the model as incredibly slow, taking over 14 seconds to respond to simple prompts like "Sat Hi". Even stranger, when prompted with "Hello," the model started solving a Pythagorean theorem problem that wasn’t part of the input. Interestingly, a larger Mistral Nemo Instruct 12B model (Q4_K_S quantization) ran much faster on the same hardware. This raises several questions: Could the Q6_K_L quantization or LM Studio configuration be causing these performance and behavior issues? Are there known quirks with Qwen3-8B’s runtime on TitanXP GPUs? Has anyone else observed similar delays or unexpected math computations in Qwen3-8B or comparable models? Sharing your setup details or troubleshooting tips might help clarify if this is a hardware, software, or model-related bottleneck.
